articles.description:
For the past few days, 7 Inkscape Members met up in Frankfurt, Germany to collaborate on various projects and get to know each other.


We were especially delighted to have two InkStitch maintainers, a major downstream project of Inkscape, join us. This way, we got to learn about the struggles and worries of projects using Inkscape better, and even built a new capability for extensions to interact with Inkscape during the event.


Marc, our release manager, cleared out our merge request backlog, reviewing and merging various contributions. He also set up a new web-based translation service, so that translators don't have to learn how to use git, and we hopefully see better Inkscape translations in many languages. He also collaborated with Vaibhav on getting the handles behave well when…
articles.title: Inkscape Summit Frankfurt 2025

sources.title: Articles on Smashing Magazine — For Web Designers And Developers

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Eduard Kuric)
articles.description: Eduard Kuric discusses the significance and role of context in the creation of relevant follow-up questions for unmoderated usability testing, how an AI tasked with interactive follow-up should be validated for its capability to incorporate such context, and what the potential — along with the risks — of AI interaction in usability testing.
articles.title: Human-Centered Design Through AI-Assisted Usability Testing: Reality Or Fiction?

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Eric Burel)
articles.description: The OWASP vulnerabilities list is the perfect starting point for web developers looking to strengthen their security expertise. Let’s discover how these vulnerabilities materialize in full-stack web applications and how to prevent them.
articles.title: How OWASP Helps You Secure Your Full-Stack Web Applications

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Vitaly Friedman)
articles.description: The goal of content design is to reduce confusion and improve clarity. Yet often it’s difficult to pinpoint a problem as user feedback tends to be not specific enough. But: we can use a few simple techniques to assess how users understand and perceive content. Let’s take a look. Part of [How To Measure UX & Design Impact](https://measure-ux.com/) by yours truly.
articles.title: How To Test And Measure Content In UX

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Matt Zeunert)
articles.description: Optimizing web performance means looking beyond surface-level metrics. Time to First Byte (TTFB) is crucial, but improving it requires more than tweaking server response time. Matt Zeunert breaks down what TTFB is, what causes its poor score, and why reducing server response time alone isn’t enough for optimization and often won’t be the most impactful change you can make to your website.
articles.title: Time To First Byte: Beyond Server Response Time

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Tomasz Jakut)
articles.description: Tomasz Jakut reflects on the evolution of web design, from the days of table-based layouts and Flash games to the rise of responsive web design (RWD), which often feels like the end of history in web layout. But as 2025 marks the 15th anniversary of Ethan Marcotte’s article, it’s worth asking whether something significant happened after RWD — something so seamless that it went almost unnoticed.
articles.title: Taking RWD To The Extreme

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Edoardo Dusi)
articles.description: In today’s web development landscape, the concept of a monolithic application has become increasingly rare. Modern applications are composed of multiple specialized services, each of which handles specific aspects of functionality. This shift didn’t happen overnight - it’s the result of decades of evolution in how we think about and implement data transfer between systems. Let’s explore this journey and see how it shapes modern architectures, particularly in the context of headless CMS solutions.
articles.title: Integrations: From Simple Data Transfer To Modern Composable Architectures

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Cosima Mielke)
articles.description: Let’s make the most of the shortest of all months, with a new collection of desktop wallpapers celebrating new opportunities, sweet memories, happy little moments, and everything in between. All of them created with love by the community for the community. Enjoy!
articles.title: Look Closer, Inspiration Lies Everywhere (February 2025 Wallpapers Edition)

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Paul Boag)
articles.description: Design systems play a crucial role in today’s digital landscape, providing a blueprint for consistent and user-friendly interfaces. But there’s another tool that deserves equal attention: the digital playbook.
articles.title: The Digital Playbook: A Crucial Counterpart To Your Design System

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Brecht De Ruyte)
articles.description: It’s not always the big features that make our everyday lives easier; sometimes, it’s those ease-of-life features that truly enhance our projects. In this article, Brecht De Ruyte highlights two such features: `@starting-style` and `transition-behavior` — two properties that are absolutely welcome additions to your everyday work with CSS animations.
articles.title: Transitioning Top-Layer Entries And The Display Property In CSS

articles.author: hello@smashingmagazine.com (Frederick O’Brien)
articles.description: After months of anticipation, debate, and even a bit of apprehension, Svelte 5 arrived earlier this year. Frederick O’Brien caught up with its creator, Rich Harris, to talk about the path that brought him and his team here and what lies ahead.

  • På plattformen Truth social skriver USA:s president Donald Trump att det "är en bra dag för Tyskland”.
articles.title: Kristersson ser fram emot samarbete med Tyskland

• Påve Franciskus har dubbelsidig lunginflammation och nedsatt njurfunktion och ligger sedan drygt en vecka inlagd på ett sjukhus i Rom.

articles.description:

• Masskjutningen i Örebro kan väcka gamla trauman hos personer med erfarenhet av till exempel krig.

  • ”Jag har märkt att vissa av våra patienter har påverkats väldigt negativt av den här händelsen och att man har blivit mer orolig och mer stressad”, säger Niklas Möller, psykolog och verksamhetschef på Röda Korset.

  • ”Jag behöver stöd då och då känner jag”, säger 35-åriga Fatima som var inne på Campus Risbergska under skjutningen.

articles.description:
• Länsstyrelserna får skärpta krav på att kunna flytta stora delar av befolkningen inom Sverige om vi skulle hamna i krig.

  • I vår ska Myndigheten för samhällsskydd och beredskap och Försvarsmakten ge besked om att vissa län, till exempel de med mycket försvarsverksamhet, ska kunna inleda utrymning av civila så snabbt som inom fyra timmar efter beslut.

  • I dessa län ska alla som behöver hjälp evakueras inom tre dygn.
articles.title: Kraven på snabb massutrymning vid krig skärps i Sverige

articles.description:
• På lördagen skulle över 600 palestinska fångar ha släppts ur israeliska fängelser inom ramen för den sköra vapenvilan där Hamas släppte sex gisslan. Men de palestinska fångarna släpptes inte.

  • Det är en protest mot Hamas förödmjukande ceremonier vid gisslanutlämning, något som Netanyahu kallar ”Hamas brott mot överenskommelsen”, enligt Cecilia Uddén, Sveriges Radios Mellanösternkorrespondent.

  • ”Det finns bedömare som misstänker att Netanyahu har andra motiv till detta, att han vill sabotera den kommande fasen av vapenvilan för att återuppta kriget”, säger Cecilia Uddén.
articles.title: Uddén: Därför släpper inte Israel de 600 palestinska fångarna

articles.description:
Video: 
			00:00:40
				
Back in 2023, we reported on Solar Orbiter’s discovery of tiny jets near the Sun’s south pole that could be powering the solar wind. The team behind this research has now used even more data from the European Space Agency’s prolific solar mission to confirm that these jets exist all over dark patches in the Sun’s atmosphere, and that they really are a source of not only fast but also slow solar wind.
The newfound jets can be seen in this sped-up video as hair-like wisps that flash very briefly, for example within the circled regions of the Sun's surface. In reality they last around one minute and fling out charged particles at about 100 km/s.
The surprising result is published today in Astronomy & Astrophysics, highlighting how Solar Orbiter’s unique combination of…
articles.title: Scientists spot tiny Sun jets driving fast and slow solar wind

articles.description:
Video: 
			00:01:40
				
Using data from the European Space Agency’s Gaia mission, scientists have found a huge exoplanet and a brown dwarf. This is the first time a planet has been uniquely discovered by Gaia’s ability to sense the gravitational tug or ‘wobble’ the planet induces on a star. Both the planet and brown dwarf are orbiting low-mass stars, a scenario thought to be extremely rare.
Read more.
Access the related animations: Gaia-4b / Gaia-5b
Access the related broadcast quality video material.
articles.title: ESA’s Gaia finds a mysterious planet and brown dwarf
Wobbling stars reveal hidden companions in Gaia data
